program_version.source_prose: The seven required courses (five in economics, one in statistics, and one in mathematics) plus seven electives within economics (which may, under certain circumstances, include a limited number of courses from related disciplines) constitute the major.
program_version.admission_prose: To declare a major in economics, a student must have a grade of C or better in both 01:220:102 Introduction to Microeconomics and 01:220:103 Introduction to Macroeconomics. The student must also have completed the required calculus course with a grade of C or better.

requirements.name: Economics Major
requirements.source_prose: The seven required courses (five in economics, one in statistics, and one in mathematics) plus seven electives within economics (which may, under certain circumstances, include a limited number of courses from related disciplines) constitute the major.

requirements.name: Required Economics Courses
requirements.source_prose: The foundation of the curriculum in economics consists of 01:220:102,103, 320, 321, and 322.

requirements.name: Statistics
requirements.source_prose: It also requires one semester of statistics (01:960:211 or preferably 285) with a grade of C or better.

requirements.name: Calculus
requirements.source_prose: One semester of calculus (01:640:135 or equivalent) with a grade of C or better also is required.
requirements.notes: 'or equivalent' is not modeled: the page does not name the equivalents (01:640:151 is the obvious candidate, but the page does not say so).

requirements.name: Economics Electives (seven)
requirements.notes: Any undergraduate 01:220 course other than the required ones, plus the two accounting courses the page names. OVER-APPROXIMATION: the 'no more than three lower-level electives' limit depends on each course's prerequisites and is not modeled; 'related disciplines' courses are not named and are not encoded.
requirements.source_prose: plus seven electives within economics (which may, under certain circumstances, include a limited number of courses from related disciplines) ... Students may take 33:010:272 and 275. These courses will count toward the required seven electives

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Students can count no more than three courses that have no prerequisites, or whose prerequisites are only 01:220:102 and 103 (or only 200), toward the seven required electives.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Classifying a course as 'lower-level' needs its prerequisite structure; Phase 6.2 parses prerequisites but the requirement layer does not use them.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Engineering students who take 01:220:200 use it in place of 01:220:102 and 103 and take eight electives instead of seven.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: A school-dependent alternative that also changes the elective count; not representable without a student-attribute condition.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: A maximum of three economics courses taken outside the Department of Economics at Rutgers University-New Brunswick may be applied toward the major.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Course location/transfer provenance is not recorded on StudentCourse.

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 in the major; C or better in the required courses; only one elective with a grade of D.
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Minimum grades and GPA are out of scope (Phase 6.3).

rules_not_yet_modeled.rule: Students who major in economics (220) may not minor in environmental and business economics (373).
rules_not_yet_modeled.why_not: Cross-program restrictions are out of scope.
